facts.text: On this date in 1781, a group of 44 settlers founded a small pueblo on the California coast. That settlement is now Los Angeles, the second-largest city in the United States.
On September 4, 1888, George Eastman patented the Kodak camera — a device so simple its slogan was 'you press the button, we do the rest.' It democratized photography within a decade.
Monaco is smaller than New York's Central Park, yet it has the world's highest GDP per capita and a longer life expectancy than any other nation on Earth.
More people live inside a 40-kilometer radius of Tokyo than in the entire country of Canada. The greater Tokyo area holds roughly 37 million people.
The country with the most time zones is France — not Russia or the United States. French overseas territories spread it across 12 distinct zones simultaneously.
On Sept 4, 1998, Google incorporated with $100,000 in seed money. It now generates more than that every 90 seconds in profit.
On Sept 4, 1929, stock prices began their pre-crash slide — the Dow would lose 89% of its value before bottoming out in 1932.
The S&P 500 has closed higher on the Friday before Labor Day more than 70% of the time since 1950 — the most reliable single-day seasonal bias in U.S. equities.
Saudi Aramco briefly hit a $2 trillion market cap in 2022. The entire U.S. banking sector — every bank combined — was worth less.
The Dutch East India Company paid a dividend every single year for nearly 200 years, even while actively losing wars and going bankrupt in 1799.

On this date in 1998, Google was incorporated — but the universe already contained a search engine of sorts: your brain executes roughly 100 trillion synaptic operations per second, dwarfing any server farm on Earth.

On September 4, 1882, Edison switched on the first commercial power grid in Manhattan. The electrons powering it moved at under 1mm per second — the energy traveled fast, but the actual particles barely shuffled.
A teaspoon of neutron star material weighs about 10 million tons. The star itself is essentially one enormous atomic nucleus, held together by the same force binding protons in your cells.
Your skeleton is not the fixed scaffold it appears. Every atom of calcium in your bones will be completely replaced within roughly 10 years, making you a slow, continuous act of self-construction.
Light slows down inside a diamond to 124,000 km/s — about 41% of its vacuum speed. That trapped, redirected light is the entire reason a cut stone appears to brilliantly glow from within.
On this day in 1998, Google was incorporated in a Menlo Park garage. It is younger than the Furby.
On this day in 1781, settlers founded a village called El Pueblo de Los Ángeles. The U.S. Constitution didn't exist yet.
Oxford University was teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. It predates Tenochtitlán by roughly two centuries.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
Nintendo was founded in 1889, making it older than the Eiffel Tower, sliced bread, and commercial air travel.
Saudade (Portuguese): a melancholic longing for something beloved and lost. Untranslatable, it sits between grief and pleasure — the ache of loving what is absent.
Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word for the look shared by two people who both want something but hope the other will act first. One word; an entire negotiation.
Hiraeth (Welsh): homesickness for a home you cannot return to — or never had. It carries grief, longing, and incompleteness in a single breath.
On this date in 1888, George Eastman patented the Kodak camera, coining its name because he wanted a word that was short, pronounceable in any language, and meant nothing at all.
Kenopsia: the eerie, forlorn quality of a place usually bustling but now abandoned. Coined recently, yet it names something humans have always felt stepping into an empty school or silent office.

On this date in 2017, China's central bank declared ICOs illegal and ordered all proceeds returned to investors — triggering a 20% single-day drop in ETH and accelerating the offshore migration of the entire token-sale industry.

On September 4, 2020, SushiSwap's anonymous founder Chef Nomi returned $14M in ETH after publicly admitting he had drained the developer fund, one of the few cases of a rug-pull being voluntarily reversed.

Bitcoin's UTXO model means your wallet holds no coins — it holds cryptographic proofs that unspent transaction outputs are spendable by your key. The 'balance' shown in software is computed on the fly.

The Ethereum genesis block was mined on July 30, 2015, but contained 8,893 pre-allocated addresses funded via the 2014 presale — meaning ETH was never a purely proof-of-work-originated asset from block one.

Satoshi's original Bitcoin whitepaper never uses the word 'blockchain' — the structure is described as a 'chain of blocks', and the compound noun became industry standard only years after Satoshi's disappearance.

On this date in 2009, Fei-Fei Li's team began the final push to release ImageNet — 14 million labeled images that would make the 2012 AlexNet breakthrough possible and effectively start the modern deep learning era.
Today in 2017, Google Brain published the Transformer paper. 'Attention Is All You Need' had eight authors; seven left Google within five years to found or co-found competing AI labs.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed more compute than all AI research published before 2012 combined — a compression of roughly six decades of academic progress into a single model.

AlphaFold 2 predicted the structures of over 200 million proteins before most structural biologists had personally determined 200. The entire Protein Data Bank took 50 years to accumulate 170,000 entries.

The first neural network to defeat a human grandmaster at chess wasn't Deep Blue — it was a 1991 system called NETchess running on hardware weaker than a modern thermostat. Deep Blue used brute-force search, not learned weights.
